chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

In chaotic disturbances there is no blood-money liability upon the ʿāqilah and no qiṣāṣ. The hāʾishāt are a panic that occurs at night, in which a man may be wounded in the head, or a slain person may be found and it is not known who killed him or wounded him.

key_terms.الْهَائِشَاتِ: chaotic disturbances or panicked tumult in which harm occurs amid confusion
key_terms.عَقْلٌ: blood-money liability borne by the killer’s ʿāqilah
key_terms.قِصَاصٌ: retaliatory legal punishment for intentional bodily injury or killing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person killed or injured in a chaotic crowd or nighttime panic when the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning injuries and deaths that occur in sudden nighttime panic and confusion where the perpetrator cannot be identified. In such cases, qiṣāṣ and liability of the ʿāqilah do not apply, because responsibility cannot be assigned to a known killer or assailant.
